# 07.4 · GeniOS desktop app — the Rust core, commented out

**Written for:** Harsh and any coding agent working on the Mac app; Rohit, to keep and hand over. This is the part you don't see: the Tauri app that owns sign-in, the Keychain, screen reading, the popup queue, the sound, and every call to the brain.

**What this is:** 71 source files, 22,459 lines, exactly as they stand in the dashboard repo at commit `ed2724d` (branch `rohit/desktop-ux`, GeniOS 0.3.4, 23 Oct 2026). Paths are relative to `Extension/`, except `src/lib/…`, which sits at the dashboard repo's root and is shared with the website.

**It does not run from here, on purpose.** Every line starts with `// ` (shell, Python, TOML and YAML lines with `# `), so nothing in this file can be imported, built or executed by accident. What the code does, and where everything is, is in [`00-README.md`](00-README.md). How it was built, step by step, is in [`02-HOW-IT-WAS-BUILT.md`](02-HOW-IT-WAS-BUILT.md).

**To get the files back** (into an empty folder, never into a repo by accident):

```bash
mkdir -p /tmp/genios-app && cd /tmp/genios-app
python3 - "<path to this file>" <<'PY'
import os, re, sys
text = open(sys.argv[1]).read()
for path, body in re.findall(r"^#### `([^`]+)`\n\n```[a-z]*\n(.*?)\n```", text, re.S | re.M):
    pre = "# " if path.rsplit(".", 1)[-1].lstrip(".") in ("py", "sh", "toml", "yaml", "yml", "gitignore") or path.endswith(".gitignore") else "// "
    lines = [l[len(pre):] if l.startswith(pre) else l[len(pre.rstrip()):] for l in body.split("\n")]
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(path) or ".", exist_ok=True)
    open(path, "w").write("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
PY
```

```toml
# serde = { version = "1.0", features = ["derive"] }
# log = "0.4"
# tauri = { version = "2.11.3", features = ["macos-private-api", "tray-icon", "image-png"] }
# tauri-plugin-log = "2"
# tauri-plugin-global-shortcut = "2"
# tauri-plugin-http = "2"
# # Opens the device-code approval page in the default browser (Rust-side only; no JS permission).
# tauri-plugin-opener = "2"
# # All below are already in the Tauri dependency tree at these versions.
# tokio = { version = "1", features = ["sync", "time", "macros", "rt", "process"] }
# chrono = { version = "0.4", default-features = false, features = ["clock", "std", "serde"] }
# sha2 = "0.10"
# hex = "0.4"
# getrandom = "0.3"
# url = "2"
# # Screen reader text rules (uia/): already in the dependency tree at 1.13.
# regex = "1"
#
# # Capture platform (plan §10) on macOS and Windows: SQLCipher store, gzip uploads, hot lane.
# # Kept out of Linux builds so that target compiles exactly as before.
# # Windows (MSVC) builds of the vendored OpenSSL under SQLCipher need Perl (Strawberry Perl is on
# # GitHub's windows runners) and use NASM for the assembly when it is on PATH (else `no-asm`).
# [target.'cfg(any(target_os = "macos", target_os = "windows"))'.dependencies]
# rusqlite = { version = "0.37", features = ["bundled-sqlcipher-vendored-openssl"] }
# flate2 = "1"
# # Hot lane (P3): slice-alias matching. Already in the dependency tree (via regex) at 1.1.5.
# aho-corasick = "1"
#
# # macOS only: Keychain and the genios-ax sidecar (Windows reads through UI Automation instead).
# [target.'cfg(target_os = "macos")'.dependencies]
# keyring-core = "1"
# tauri-plugin-shell = "2"
# apple-native-keyring-store = { version = "1", features = ["keychain"] }
#
# [dev-dependencies]
# wiremock = "0.6"
# tokio = { version = "1", features = ["sync", "time", "macros", "rt", "rt-multi-thread", "test-util"] }
# tempfile = "3"
#
# # Foreground-window reading, per OS. Both crates are already in the Tauri dependency
# # tree at these versions, so declaring them costs no extra compile.
# [target.'cfg(target_os = "windows")'.dependencies]
# windows = { version = "0.61", features = [
#   "Win32_Foundation",
#   "Win32_System_Threading",
#   "Win32_UI_WindowsAndMessaging",
#   # Screen reader (uia/source.rs): UI Automation over COM.
#   "Win32_UI_Accessibility",
#   "Win32_System_Com",
```

## 3 · Sign-in and secrets

Device sign-in (RFC 8628), the session, and the Keychain (with the once-per-run cache).

#### `src-tauri/src/auth/client.rs`

// //! Device sign-in and session tokens (P1 WP4; contract: P1 build §3.1).
// //!
// //! State machine
// //! ```text
// //!   signed_out ──start──▶ pending ──approved──▶ signed_in ──refresh 401/403──▶ signed_out
// //!                           │  └─denied──▶ denied            │
// //!                           └─expired──▶ expired             └─sign_out / DEVICE_REVOKED──▶ signed_out
// //! ```
// //! * The refresh token (+ the device id it is bound to and the engine URL) is the only thing
// //!   persisted, in the platform [`SecretStore`] (Keychain on macOS).
// //! * The access token lives in memory only. It is refreshed shortly before expiry, and after a
// //!   401 via [`AuthManager::refresh_if_stale`] — single-flight, because rotation invalidates the
// //!   presented refresh token (a second concurrent refresh would look like reuse and revoke us).
// //! * Any definitive 401/403 from `/auth/refresh` (`REFRESH_REUSED`, `SEAT_INACTIVE`,
// //!   `SESSION_REVOKED`, …) ends the session locally; network errors keep it.

## 4 · Screen reading

The genios-ax supervisor, the privacy gate, timing, sessions, the encrypted on-device store, uploads, policy, presence, reader health.

```rust
// //! Reader health — the forbidden state is silence (plan NFR-04).
// //!
// //! A dedicated reader is a single-vendor UI dependency. WhatsApp ships an update on a Tuesday
// //! night, one accessibility path moves, `WhatsAppReader` finds no message list — and today the
// //! outcome is nothing at all: no reads, no checks, no items, no cost, an empty panel. A manager
// //! reads that as "it stopped finding things", not "it stopped seeing WhatsApp", and the first
// //! person to notice is whoever is demoing.
// //!
// //! So a reader that used to see content and now sees none says so. The rule is deliberately
// //! narrow — two conditions, both required, and only for an app that HAS worked on this machine:
// //!
// //! * `EMPTY_RUNS` reads in a row with nothing in them (a chat really can be empty once), and
// //! * `QUIET_AFTER` since the last time that app gave us anything (a quick glance at an empty
// //!   window is not a broken reader).
// //!
// //! Any content at all clears it. Nothing here changes what is captured or sent: it is a sentence
// //! in the panel and a flag in `capture_status`.

// use std::collections::HashMap;
```

```rust
// //! Diff, dedupe and session buffering (plan §10.6 "Diff and dedupe", "Session buffer and flush").
// //!
// //! * identical tree hash ⇒ skip the read entirely;
// //! * per-message fingerprint = sha256(normalised sender | normalised text | thread key) ⇒ novel vs seen;
// //! * per-thread watermark = ordinal of the last message seen in that thread;
// //! * session = (thread_key, local hour bucket); rollover freezes the old one;
// //! * flush (= hand a delta to the persistent upload queue) on: thread switch, 5 min after the
// //!   first new message, hour rollover, 40 messages / 6 000 chars pending, quit, idle/lock/sleep,
// //!   manual "sync now";
// //! * scrolled up (only older messages visible) ⇒ nothing is captured;
// //! * ≤ 6 context messages precede each delta; the draft rides along only with Draft assist on.
// //!
// //! Generic reader (`screen_doc`, plan §10.7): per-block fingerprint (normalised text + role +
// //! path, scoped to the thread), only new/changed blocks upload, plus ≤ 10 context blocks; the
// //! thread key is bundle id + normalised URL path, or the window title for native apps. Same
// //! sessions and flush rules. Caps per read: 30k chars, 500 blocks, 200 table rows.

// //! Each delta has its own `message_watermark`, so `(device_id, session_key, message_watermark)`
```

```rust
// //! Where thread reads come from (P1 build §3.6). Readers only READ; fingerprints, watermarks,
// //! sessions and flush rules are owned by `session.rs`.
// //!
// //! * [`SidecarThreadSource`] runs `genios-ax read --frontmost [--draft]` (one `screen_doc` line from
// //!   the structured generic reader; dedicated readers later emit `thread_read` on the same call).
// //!   `--draft` is passed only while Draft assist is on. An older sidecar without `read` is
// //!   detected once ("unknown command") and every later call returns [`ReadOutcome::Unsupported`].
// //! * [`FixtureThreadSource`] replays JSON fixtures (tests, and a stand-in until WP5 lands).
// //!
// //! A read is either a dedicated reader's `thread_read` (§3.6) or the structured generic
// //! reader's `screen_doc` (§3.7, plan §10.7) — [`ScreenRead`].
```

```rust
// //! the capture service consumes on macOS, produced natively and fed through the service's
// //! existing [`WatchSpawner`](super::supervisor::WatchSpawner) seam — so the actor, gate,
// //! scheduler, sessions, presence and uploads run unchanged.
// //!
// //! * foreground app / window / title → `app_activated` / `focused_window_changed` /
// //!   `title_changed` (WinEvent `EVENT_SYSTEM_FOREGROUND` + window `EVENT_OBJECT_NAMECHANGE`,
// //!   and a 1 s poll as a safety net). Browsers also carry the page URL (UI Automation), so the
// //!   gate can refuse a sensitive site BEFORE anything on it is read.
// //! * content / typing → `value_changed` (`EVENT_OBJECT_VALUECHANGE` / `EVENT_OBJECT_REORDER` in
// //!   the foreground process, rate-limited), focus → `focused_element_changed` with an AX-style
// //!   role so the core's composer rule (`is_composer_role`) works as on macOS.
// //! * idle (`GetLastInputInfo`, 120 s like the sidecar), lock (the input desktop cannot be
// //!   opened while the workstation is locked or a secure desktop is up), sleep (a wall-clock jump
// //!   between polls) → `idle_start`/`idle_end`, `screen_locked`/`screen_unlocked`,
// //!   `system_sleep` + `system_wake`.
```

## 5 · The popups

The lane window, its queue (five seconds, hover hold, quiet, pacing) and the popup sound.

#### `src-tauri/src/lane/queue.rs`

```rust
// //! Lane toast queue (plan §6.1 step 8, §6.0 reminder vs intelligence). Pure logic, no UI.
// //!
// //! * Never more than one toast visible. Next = highest priority; at equal priority reminders
// //!   before advice; then first come.
// //! * Pending reminders merge into one toast when shown.
// //! * Org policy `moments_display:false` (shadow mode) ⇒ nothing is ever shown, whatever the
// //!   moment says; `display:false` on a moment (server rate limit / quiet hours) ⇒ not shown.
// //! * Quiet (device DND or capture paused) shows only `critical`: non-critical advice is dropped,
// //!   reminders are held and shown once quiet ends (while still inside their TTL).
// //! * Device-origin advice is capped locally at 6/hour and 30/day (same defaults as the server,
// //!   §2.2) so an offline device cannot spam.
// //! * Reminders are never DROPPED (§6.0 — a reminder is the person's own promise, and a cap that
// //!   silently discards one is worse than the flood). They are PACED: at most one reminder toast
// //!   every `REMINDER_GAP_MS`, and everything that arrives inside that gap merges into the next
// //!   toast instead of each getting its own interruption. Nothing is lost — the gap is well
// //!   inside every reminder's 1800 s TTL — and `High` / `Critical` reminders (a meeting about to
// //!   start) skip the gap entirely.
// //!
// //!   "Never rate-limited" used to mean "no limit at all", and the measured worst hour (9 Oct
// //!   2026 12:00 UTC) was 22 reminder-kind moments for one seat: 19 follow-up nudges, 2 chat-open
// //!   cards, 1 due-today digest, nine of them inside eleven seconds. A person who reads and
// //!   clears each toast got 22 interruptions in an hour.
// //! * Every popup shows five seconds, with a line along its top that runs out with the time
// //!   (Rohit, 22 Oct 2026: a popup that stayed until acted on was a popup nobody could get rid
// //!   of). Hovering holds it; leaving starts the five seconds again. Nothing is lost when it
// //!   goes: a follow-up stays in the menu's Pending, a card on the website, and every popup in
// //!   the menu's Screen history. An agent proposal is the one exception — it waits for
// //!   Approve / Edit / Reject (max 10 min) or its TTL.
// //! * P9 K8: one screen insight (`moment.screen_insight`) at a time. Other insights wait behind
// //!   it (their TTL applies while waiting). Anything else that becomes due goes first: the
// //!   insight steps back to the front of the queue and returns when that toast is done. Quiet
// //!   hides it and brings it back afterwards.

//
//     /// The measured hour, replayed through the real queue (9 Oct 2026 12:00 UTC, one seat).
//     ///
//     /// 22 moments, every one `kind: reminder`, which `offer` exempts from the device cap: 19
//     /// `moment.followup`, 2 `moment.chat_open`, 1 `moment.due_today`. The arrival times are the
//     /// `created_at` of those rows, to the second — bursts of nine inside eleven seconds, then the
//     /// same follow-ups again at 12:45 and 12:55.
//     ///
//     /// The person here is the one the cap exists for: they read each toast and clear it. Merging
//     /// only helps someone who leaves toasts alone, so a diligent manager is the worst case, and
//     /// counting toasts is counting interruptions.
//     const MEASURED_HOUR: [(i64, &str); 22] = [
//         (1, "followup"), (75, "due_today"), (816, "chat_open"), (835, "chat_open"),
//         (1201, "followup"), (1202, "followup"), (1203, "followup"), (1204, "followup"),
//         (1800, "followup"), (1803, "followup"), (1804, "followup"), (1805, "followup"),
//         (1806, "followup"), (1808, "followup"), (1809, "followup"), (1809, "followup"),
//         (1810, "followup"), (1811, "followup"),
//         (2708, "followup"), (3310, "followup"), (3311, "followup"), (3312, "followup"),
//     ];
//
//     /// Replay the measured hour second by second, the way the service runs it (`service.rs`
//     /// ticks the lane once a second), and keep ticking afterwards until the queue is empty.
//     ///
//     /// Returns (toasts inside the measured hour, moments delivered in the end). The two are
//     /// counted over different windows on purpose: interruptions are what the hour cost the
//     /// person, and delivery is a promise with no deadline in this test — a reminder that arrives
//     /// at 12:55 and is shown at 13:00 was not lost, and a bound that pretends otherwise would
//     /// measure the replay window instead of the system.
```

## 6 · Moments: what pops up and why

The hot lane on the device: reminders, follow-ups, brief and wrap, situations, delegation, the delivery ledger.

```rust
// //! P-21 attention — the one card that is about where the manager is NOT looking.
// //!
// //! Every other moment answers "what is on this screen?". This one answers the opposite: the
// //! manager has been on one surface for half an hour while something with a clock on it sits
// //! open somewhere else. A customer escalation waits two hours because the Q3 doc is absorbing;
// //! nothing on the screen can say that, and no model is needed to know it.
// //!
// //! It is entirely arithmetic on the slice — dwell, a due date, a thread key — so it costs
// //! nothing and can be verified the way the server's interrupt gate verifies its five reasons:
// //!
// //! * the same surface has been in focus, uninterrupted, for `DWELL_MINUTES`;
// //! * an OPEN follow-up is due within `SOON_MINUTES` or is already past due;
// //! * that follow-up is about a different thread (chasing you about the thing you are already
// //!   doing is not attention, it is noise);
// //! * it was not already raised — once per item, and at most one of these per `REPEAT_HOURS`.
```

```rust
// //! Moment endpoints (P3 build §2.2–§2.4) over the device-authenticated capture client, plus an
// //! ordered outbox for fire-and-forget writes (device moments, feedback). The outbox keeps
// //! order (a device moment is posted before its feedback), retries transient failures with
// //! backoff, drops 4xx, and empties on sign-out. It is saved to the encrypted capture store after
// //! every change, so ops pending at quit are sent on the next start (the store is wiped on
// //! sign-out, so nothing crosses accounts).
```

// //! THE DELIVERY LEDGER — "have we already said this, and has the answer changed since?"
// //!
// //! That one question had no owner. Ten mechanisms across four modules each re-derived a piece of
// //! it with its own key and its own clock (`tree_hash`, `block_fingerprint`, `watermark`,
// //! `insight_seen`, `checked`, two four-hour cooldowns, the server's moment TTL, the thread verdict,
// //! the topic cap), and the pieces that mattered most for repetition — `ChatOpen.shown`,
// //! `attention`, `checked`, `sent` — lived in RAM, so quitting the app made every card new again.
// //!
// //! MEASURED on one seat, 3–10 Oct 2026: the same headline was produced five times over 26 hours
// //! (`With Anshika: Follow up with Anshika on invitation sent`), five times over 16 hours
// //! (`Monday (12 Oct): you have a meeting at 11:30 AM`), four times over four hours
// //! (`Asmit Banik · supymem.com — last touch 3 d ago`). None of those was a bug: `quick.rs`
// //! re-shows a thread `CHAT_OPEN_REPEAT_SECS` (four hours) after the last time, whether or not
// //! anything about it changed. A clock sits where a comparison belongs.
// //!
// //! ## What this module is, and is not
// //!
// //! It answers *delivery* questions only. Capture's dedupe — did the SCREEN change — stays exactly
// //! where it is and keeps its names; so does the P12 ladder, where three deliveries of one dated
// //! promise (heads-up → final → overdue) are three different things, not a repeat.
// //!
// //! ## Phase 0 (this file today): observability, and no behaviour change at all
// //!
// //! Every decision the lane already makes is written to `delivery_log` with the reason it already
// //! has. Nothing reads the log yet and no decision changes. That ordering is deliberate: the plan
// //! replaces two load-bearing cooldowns, and without a before-and-after measurement there is no way
// //! to tell a fix from a regression. `scripts/delivery_report.py` reads it.
// //!
// //! ## Phase 1: the same decisions, remembered across a restart
// //!
// //! Five maps decided "have we shown this lately" and all five lived in RAM, so quitting the app
// //! re-showed everything: `ChatOpen.shown` (the largest producer), `attention.raised`,
// //! `local_keys`, `p02_last` and `insight_seen`. [`remember`] / [`recall`] put them in the
// //! encrypted store under five scopes of one table. Same rules, same thresholds, same call sites —
// //! the only difference is that closing the lid is no longer an instruction to repeat yourself.
// //!
// //! `checked` and `sent` are deliberately NOT here. They key on `Instant`, a monotonic clock with
// //! no meaning after a restart, so persisting them means moving them to wall time — a behaviour
// //! change, and it belongs in phase 2 where that comparison is rebuilt anyway.

// //! `watermark`). The two keys below are what makes that possible, which is why they are computed

//
// /// Does the ledger get to judge this card at all?
// ///
// /// MEASURED on the 315 moments one seat produced 3–10 Oct 2026. 277 of them name their subject
// /// in an action payload — `moment.chat_open` (133, follow-up id), `moment.followup` (109),
// /// `moment.attention` (27) and `moment.screen_insight` (8, thread key). The other 38 name
// /// nothing, and `subject_of` falls back to the capability id for them, which is fine for a log
// /// and wrong for a decision: every `moment.reminder` would share one subject and the second one
// /// would be suppressed as a repeat of the first.
// ///
// /// So: no named subject, no suppression. That is not a concession, it is the right rule — the
// /// capabilities with no subject are `daily_brief`, `daily_wrap` and `due_today`, which are
// /// digests that MUST come back every day and whose claim can legitimately be identical two
// /// mornings running.
// ///
// /// Two more exemptions, both of them cases where repeating is the point:
// /// * an agent proposal the person asked for a moment ago (plan §2.1 rule 4, "the person asked");
// /// * a local notice ("Draft copied") — UI feedback on an action, with the same words every time
// ///   by design.
// pub fn judges(m: &Moment) -> bool {
//     !m.awaits_decision() && !m.capability_id.starts_with("moment.local_notice") && names_a_subject(m)
// }

```rust
// //! P-18 reminders from local timers (plan §6.0 "Reminders and intelligence are two separate
// //! systems"): the schedule comes from the slice, the device fires on the minute — offline too.
// //!
// //! * Meeting soon: `start_at − 15 min` (skipped once the meeting started). P5: when it fires the
// //!   service asks `POST /v1/moments/evaluate` with `features.meeting_node_id` for the server's
// //!   prep moment (P-15) and shows that; on 204 / offline / hidden it shows this local toast.
// //! * Commitment due: `due_at − 60 min`, only for commitments the seat owes (`owner:"seat"`;
// //!   `owner:"counterparty"` ones are owed to the seat and never remind).
// //! * A timer whose moment passed more than 5 min ago (app was closed/asleep) is skipped, not
// //!   flooded. Fired keys (`node_id:fire_at`) are kept in `moments_local`, so a restart never
// //!   re-fires; a rescheduled item gets a new key and fires again.
// //! * Several due at once merge into one reminder toast.
// //! * Undated commitment the seat owes: one "Still open" nudge 3 working days after it was first
// //!   recorded (`since`), once. Its window is 7 days (the app may be closed on the day) and fired
// //!   keys are kept 10 days, so it never repeats.
// //! * P8 C7 follow-up nudge: an open slice follow-up with `nudge_at` fires once at `nudge_at`
// //!   (key `fu:{id}:{nudge_at}`, same fired store). Its window is 12 h — the morning brief
// //!   covers anything older. Its toast has Done (→ resolve `done`), Tomorrow (→ snooze
// //!   `tomorrow`), Draft reply (→ clipboard) and Dismiss.
```

#### `src-tauri/src/moments/service.rs`

```rust
// //! The hot lane on the device (plan §6.1 steps 5–8): one actor owns the slice, the matcher,
// //! reminder timers and the lane queue.
// //!
// //! * Capture read → features → P-01 locally (no network) → toast; then, if a known person or
// //!   company is in focus, `POST /v1/moments/evaluate` for P-02 (throttled per thread, 10 min).
// //! * Reminder timers (P-18) are checked every second from the local slice — they fire offline.
// //! * Every device moment is posted to `/v1/moments` (history; shadow mode still posts them) and
// //!   every shown/acted/dismissed/wrong/snoozed goes to feedback, via the ordered outbox.
// //! * Slice: loaded from the encrypted store at sign-in, pulled at start, on wake, every 15 min,
// //!   and on `slice.delta` — coalesced with a 5 s debounce (deltas come in bursts).
// //! * Sign-out / revoke: everything in memory is dropped; the store file (slice, fired keys,
// //!   Last-Event-ID) is wiped by the capture service.
// //! * P4: local P-13 / P-14 run beside P-01 (same dedupe, no network). `team` / `verify`
// //!   moments get "Open card"; verify buttons resolve the discrepancy through the outbox.
// //!   Draft assist: a changed draft is paced (≥ 1.5 s pause, ≤ 1 per 5 s) into its own
// //!   evaluate call; the review is shown copy-only, and only while its thread is in focus.
// //! * P6: "Ask my agent" proposes (`POST /v1/delegations`) and shows the exact request with
// //!   Approve / Edit / Reject; only the person's Approve click calls `/approve`. Delegation
// //!   state changes (`moment.updated` → `delegation`) show as short status toasts.
// //! * P8: follow-up nudges fire from the slice like P-18 timers (Done → resolve); the morning
// //!   brief / evening wrap fire at the first read after 05:00 / 19:00 local, once the slice is
// //!   ready this session; "Mute chat" adds the thread to a device-local muted set (capture
// //!   store) and no insight is asked for it again; the insight dedupe digest ignores UI chrome.
```

## 7 · The on-device graph slice, matcher and realtime

What the device knows about the people in your work, how it matches a screen against it, and the server's event stream.

#### `src-tauri/src/matcher/dates.rs`

```rust
// //! Date phrases in English and Hindi written in Latin script (plan §6.1 step 5). No LLM.
// //!
// //! Resolution rules (relative to `now`, in `now`'s offset):
// //! * `aaj`/`today`/`tonight` → today; `kal`/`tomorrow` → +1; `parso`/`day after tomorrow` → +2.
// //!   `kal`/`parso` followed within 4 words by a past marker (`tha`, `hua`, `gaya`, …) mean
// //!   yesterday / day before (Hindi uses one word for both directions).
// //! * A bare weekday (`friday`, `shukravar`, `fri`) = its next occurrence after today (a Monday
// //!   said on a Monday = next Monday). `this <weekday>` includes today. `next <weekday>` /
// //!   `agle <weekday>` = that weekday in next week (weeks start Monday).
// //! * `next week` / `agle hafte` → Monday of next week.
// //! * `18th` → the 18th of this month, or next month once it has passed. `18 Sep`, `Sep 18`,
```

```rust
// //! Which language a card should speak — mirrored from the manager's own words.
// //!
// //! The device already chooses language this way in one place: `moments/local.rs` writes
// //! "Kal (18 Sep) 3 pm pe meeting hai" when the DATE PHRASE the manager typed was Hinglish
// //! (`DateHit.hindi`), and the English sentence when it was not. That is the right rule — mirror
// //! the person, do not pick a house language — but it only ever applied to that one moment, so a
// //! reminder about a Hinglish promise came back in English.
// //!
// //! A card is about something somebody wrote, and that something travels with it: every follow-up
// //! carries the `quote` that caused it (P15). So the language of a card is the language of its
// //! quote. No per-seat setting to configure, no detector guessing at a person.
// //!
// //! The markers are words this device ALREADY acts on in `matcher::dates` and `matcher::intents`
// //! (Hinglish dates, and the Hinglish halves of the schedule / send / commit vocabularies). Nothing
// //! new is invented here, and `markers_are_words_the_matcher_already_knows` keeps it that way: a
// //! word in this list that the rest of the matcher does not understand is a word that drifted in.
//
// /// Hinglish markers, lower case, matched as whole tokens. None of them is an English word, so a
// /// purely English line can never match.

//     // dates (matcher::dates)

//     // send / commit / meet (matcher::intents)

//     "karenge", "karunga", "karungi", "denge", "dunga", "dungi",
//     "milte", "milna", "milo", "milenge", "mulakat", "mulaqat", "baat",

// /// Is this line the manager's Hinglish rather than their English?

// /// Hinglish, and neither has more than a couple of markers in it.
```

```rust
// //! Realtime client (P3 build §2.5): `GET /v1/stream` (SSE) with the device token.
// //!
// //! * Own HTTP client with a connect timeout only — the shared client's 20 s total timeout
// //!   would cut the stream. Silence longer than `idle` (3 missed 20 s heartbeats) = dead link.
// //! * `Last-Event-ID` is persisted by the sink (encrypted store) after every event carrying an
// //!   id and sent on every reconnect, so the server replays what was missed (kept 7 d).
// //! * Reconnect with exponential backoff + jitter (honouring the server's `retry:` as a floor),
// //!   reset after a connection that delivered data.
```

```rust
// //! On-device graph slice (P3 build §2.1, plan §6.3): `GET /v1/seats/me/slice?since=<version>`,
// //! applied as full or delta, kept in the capture SQLCipher database (tables `slice_nodes`,
// //! `slice_meta`) so it is encrypted at rest and wiped with it on sign-out / revoke.
// //!
// //! Delta semantics (pinned in P3 build §2.1, brain 414849a): `meetings`, `busy` and
// //! `commitments` are the COMPLETE current set in every response and replace wholesale;
// //! `people` and `companies` are true deltas (with a 15-min overlap — upserts are idempotent)
// //! plus `removed`.
// //!
// //! Schema v2 (P4 build §3.4) adds `companies[].other_seats` (org-visible touches by other
// //! seats, 7 d) and `recent_changes` (seat-visible field changes, ≤ 14 d). `recent_changes` is
// //! a window, so — like `meetings` — every response carries the complete current set and it
// //! replaces wholesale. v1 responses still apply (both fields empty).
// //!
// //! P8 (C5) adds `followups` (open screen follow-ups, ≤ 50, newest first) and
// //! `removed_followups` (ids resolved since `since`). They are applied as upserts + removals
// //! (right whether the server sends the complete open set or only changes). A removed follow-up
// //! is kept locally as closed for 3 days so the evening wrap can count what was kept; brief and
// //! nudges only ever look at open ones. Follow-up rows live in `slice_nodes` (kind `followup`)
// //! and are written from the applied state by [`save_followups`].
//
// use crate::capture::api::{ApiError, CaptureApi};
// use chrono::{DateTime, FixedOffset, Utc};
// use rusqlite::{params, Connection};
// use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
// use serde_json::Value;
// use std::collections::BTreeMap;
// use tauri_plugin_http::reqwest::Method;
//
// pub const SCHEMA_VERSION: u32 = 3;
// /// Oldest schema still applied (a v1 server during rollout).
// pub const MIN_SCHEMA_VERSION: u32 = 1;
//
// /// Another seat of the org already in touch with a company (v2).
// #[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
// pub struct OtherSeat {
//     #[serde(default)]
//     pub name: String,
//     #[serde(default)]
//     pub since: Option<String>,
// }
//
// /// A field whose value changed recently (v2). `old`/`new` are whatever JSON the graph holds.
// #[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
// pub struct RecentChange {
//     pub node_id: String,
//     #[serde(default)]
//     pub field: String,
//     #[serde(default)]
//     pub old: Value,
//     #[serde(default)]
```

## 8 · Windows screen reading

UI Automation in place of the macOS sidecar (Windows builds).

#### `src-tauri/src/uia/map.rs`

#### `src-tauri/src/uia/mod.rs`

```rust
// //! Screen reading without the macOS sidecar (P7 on Windows).
// //!
// //! * [`text`] / [`reader`] — the sidecar's generic reader, ported to Rust (pure, tested on every OS).
// //! * [`map`] — UI Automation elements → that reader → the same §3.7 `screen_doc`, with the
// //!   capture limits (depth 12, 5k nodes, 400 ms, 30k chars) and the dedicated-reader hook.
// //! * `source` (Windows) — [`crate::capture::thread_source::ThreadSource`] over `IUIAutomation`.
//
// pub mod map;
// pub mod reader;
// #[cfg(target_os = "windows")]
// pub mod source;
// pub mod text;
```

#### `src-tauri/src/uia/reader.rs`

```rust
// //! The structured generic reader (plan §10.7 tier 2), ported 1:1 from the macOS sidecar's
// //! `GenericReader.swift` + `ScreenDocRules` so Windows and macOS turn the same screen into the
// //! same `screen_doc`. It works on an AX-shaped tree ([`RNode`], AX role names); `uia::map` maps
// //! UI Automation elements onto those roles first.
// //!
// //! Rules (by role, never by app): headings; static text / link runs → paragraphs (a run breaks at
// //! a new line); tables/grids/outlines → header + rows; label → value pairs → kv (label element,
// //! title/description, a label text before a field, `<dl>`, a short label + value on one row);
// //! lists → list unless they look like chat (then messages, left = incoming, right = outgoing);
// //! the focused editable element → `field` + `focused_field` ONLY with Draft assist; password
// //! fields never reach here (dropped by the capture); in browsers only the page is read.
//

// use crate::capture::thread_source::{Block, BlockRole};
// use regex::Regex;
// use serde::Serialize;
// use sha2::{Digest, Sha256};
// use std::collections::HashMap;
// use std::sync::OnceLock;
```

```rust
// //! Windows screen reader: [`ThreadSource`] over UI Automation (what the `genios-ax read` sidecar
// //! is on macOS). No permission prompt — UIA is available to every desktop app.
// //!
// //! One worker thread owns COM (MTA) and a `CUIAutomation8` instance; reads are queued to it and
// //! answered within 3 s like a sidecar call. A read:
// //! 1. takes the foreground window (`GetForegroundWindow`), its process exe (the Windows "bundle
// //!    id", lower-cased: `chrome.exe`) and title; GeniOS's own windows are never read;
// //! 2. browsers: roots the read at the page `Document` (so the depth budget is spent on content),
// //!    URL = the document's Value, else the toolbar address-bar `Edit`;
// //! 3. fetches the subtree in ONE cross-process call (`BuildUpdatedCache`, `TreeScope_Subtree`,
// //!    control view) under a 400 ms UIA transaction timeout; a tree too big for that is walked
// //!    element by element instead (one call per element) inside what is left of the 400 ms;
// //! 4. hands the cached tree to `uia::map` (limits, password drop, generic reader, dedicated hook).
// //!
// //! Chromium builds its accessibility tree lazily when a UIA client first asks: a first read of a
// //! window that comes back empty is retried once after 400 ms (the sidecar's `--settle-ms`).
```
